critical_code_review_comments: landing_chatbot.py /chat (line ~140): asyncio.create_task(_score_session_lead(...)) is fire-and-forget on EVERY chat turn — even turn 1 with no email captured yet. _score_session_lead does guard with `if not lead: return`, but still makes a DB round-trip for every turn. Consider scoring only when lead was just upserted (i.e. when req.email branch fired) or when message count reaches a threshold (≥3 turns) to cut LLM cost on tire-kickers.

landing_chatbot.py _score_session_lead line parser is fragile: 'SCORE: 95/100' would parse to 95100 without the max(0,min(100,x)) clamp. The clamp saves it, but consider regex `r'^SCORE:\s*(\d{1,3})'` for robustness. TAGS parser also doesn't strip quotes or limit length — a malicious/confused LLM output like 'TAGS: very-long-tag-name-that-breaks-ui-layout' will render awkwardly in the purple chips. Recommend `t.strip()[:24]` per tag.

landing_chatbot.py /score-session is POST with `session_id` as a query param (not body) — unusual for POST; either switch to POST body (Pydantic model) or document the convention. Currently works because FastAPI accepts bare `session_id: str` as query — fine but non-obvious.

core/email.py send_email_detailed(): error message truncated to 300 chars — that's fine, but consider also logging the full error server-side (it already does via logger.error). The frontend uses .slice(0,120) on top of that so admins see ~120 chars max. Good enough for triage.
AdminLandingLeadsPage.jsx line 282: .slice(0,3) limits tags rendered to 3 — spec says 'max 4 tags' from the LLM. Either show all 4 or update spec. Minor cosmetic.

AdminLandingLeadsPage.jsx line 248-249: `isHot = score >= 70` and `isWarm = score >= 40 && score < 70` — matches the LLM CATEGORY output but there's no check that LLM's `lead_category` matches the threshold (e.g. LLM could return score=65 + category='hot'). The UI uses `score` for styling and `cat` for the 'Hot' chip, so they could disagree. Not breaking — just a consistency check.
